name: Humanoid robot pilot for passenger service at Suvarnabhumi Airport (SKY ICT)
summary: Sky ICT, the Thai company behind check-in, pre-screening, automated bag drop, automated boarding gate and biometric systems at Thai airports, said on November 2 that it will pilot humanoid robots for services inside Suvarnabhumi Airport by the end of this year, along with new smart operations centers to make ground operations more efficient. CEO Sittidej Mailap described humanoid robots that can guide passengers on airport services the way staff do, and conventional robots that help move baggage or packages on airport conveyor belts. The company frames the plan in three phases: an aviation data hub, agentic AI for personalized service and predictive maintenance, and finally a more autonomous airport using automation, biometrics and robots. No robot maker, number of units, costs or performance targets were given in the announcement.

whyItMatters: Passenger-facing robots are still pilots, not proven sales tools, but the airports trying them are testing whether a robot can answer the simple questions that tie up staff at peak times. If it works, staff are freed for the higher-value conversations that sell upgrades and services. Watch the results from Suvarnabhumi before spending on one yourself; the cheaper first step for most operators is a good chatbot.
pricing: Not applicable; pilot planned by the end of 2026
